record.context_brief: Quenched central limit behavior beyond RWRE-type models
record.original_question: Find probability measures P on cookie environments - excluding measures that merely encode ordinary random walk in random environment - such that for P-almost every environment ω, the quenched law of either the hitting time T_n or the position X_n, after whatever centering and normalization are needed, converges weakly to a nondegenerate limit distribution as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem and Example 6.17. (d ≥ 1, quenched CLT) Find measures P (not including those which model RWRE) such that for P-almost all ω the distribution under P0,ω of Tn or Xn, properly centered and normalized as needed, converges weakly to some non-degenerate distribution as n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a dimension d ≥ 1 and let M_1([0,1]^{2d}) denote the set of probability measures on [0,1]^{2d}. A cookie environment on Z^d is a map ω : Z^d → ([0,1]^{2d})^N assigning to each site x ∈ Z^d an infinite stack of "cookies" (ω(x,j))_{j≥1}, where each cookie ω(x,j) = (p_1^±(x,j), …, p_d^±(x,j)) is a probability vector on the 2d unit vectors {±e_1, …, ±e_d}. Let P be a probability measure on the space Ω of cookie environments, typically assumed to make {ω(x,·)}_{x∈Z^d} i.i.d.

Given an environment ω, the cookie (excited) random walk (X_n)_{n≥0} started at 0 is the Markov chain on Z^d under the quenched law P_{0,ω} defined as follows. If, at time n, the walker is at site x and has previously visited x exactly j−1 times, then the walker jumps to x ± e_i with probability given by the j-th cookie ω(x,j); after the jump the cookie is consumed (so the (j+1)-st cookie governs the next visit). When the stack at x has been exhausted, the walker performs nearest-neighbor steps according to a fixed (possibly site-dependent) probability vector encoded in the tail of the stack.

For d = 1, define the hitting times T_n = inf{k ≥ 0 : X_k = n}.

A measure P is said to "merely encode random walk in random environment" if, P-a.s., the cookies at each site x are constant in j (i.e. ω(x,j) does not depend on j), so that the model reduces to an ordinary RWRE.

Problem. Exhibit probability measures P on cookie environments which do not merely encode random walk in random environment, such that for P-almost every ω there exist deterministic centering sequences a_n ∈ R (or R^d) and normalizing sequences b_n > 0 for which, under the quenched law P_{0,ω}, either
(T_n − a_n)/b_n  ⟹  μ   (in the case d = 1),
or
(X_n − a_n)/b_n  ⟹  ν,
converges weakly as n → ∞ to a nondegenerate limit distribution μ (resp. ν) that does not depend on ω. Equivalently, identify nontrivial classes of genuinely "excited" cookie laws P for which a quenched (functional) central-limit-type theorem holds for the hitting times or for the position of the walk.
artifact.status_search_result: Quenched and annealed CLTs are known for several specific subclasses of excited/cookie random walks (e.g., bounded i.i.d. cookie stacks in d=1 in the ballistic regime, Markovian cookie stacks, and excited random walks in d ≥ 2 under various assumptions). However, the broader request to characterize all genuinely excited cookie laws P (beyond those reducing to RWRE) for which a quenched CLT for T_n or X_n holds does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature; partial results exist but a full classification has not been verified.

status_evidence.title: Excited random walks with Markovian cookie stacks
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes limit theorems (including CLT-type results) for cookie random walks with Markovian cookie stacks, extending classical i.i.d. cookie results.
status_evidence.claim: Quenched/annealed limit theorems are known for specific cookie-environment classes, but not in the full generality of the problem.

status_evidence.title: One-Dimensional Excited Random Walk with Unboundedly Many Cookies
status_evidence.snippet: Studies limit behavior of one-dimensional excited random walks; central limit theorems are obtained under specific assumptions on cookie distributions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial CLT results exist for special cookie distributions in d=1.

status_evidence.title: Central limit theorem for excited random walk in the recurrent regime
status_evidence.snippet: Proves a CLT for excited random walks in recurrent parameter regimes.
status_evidence.claim: CLTs known in particular regimes; broader problem of characterizing all such P remains open or unverified.
